articles.originalTitle: Medicare looks a bit different in 2027, so don't miss open enrollment
articles.originalText: Open enrollment for Medicare runs through Dec. 7, and there are a few different pitfalls people should watch out for this year. Your drug plan or Medicare Advantage plan could be changing a lot.
articles.originalFullText:
Annual open enrollment is underway for Medicare, the federal program that provides health insurance to roughly 70 million people. The coverage choices are complex and often consequential.

Open enrollment runs through Dec. 7. The plan you choose takes effect on Jan. 1, for the full calendar year.

Build-your-own Medicare menu

Medicare provides health insurance to people 65 or older, as well as to some younger people with disabilities or certain health conditions. But it isn't one plan. It's more like a build-your-own-insurance menu.

Roughly half of beneficiaries are enrolled in traditional Medicare, which consists of Parts A and B. Administered by the federal government, the plan covers hospital stays, skilled nursing care, doctor visits, outpatient care, and preventive screenings. Enrollees can typically see any healthcare provider who accepts Medicare, and they rarely need approval for diagnostic tests, such as MRIs and CT scans. However, there's no cap on out-of-pocket expenses in traditional Medicare, and it doesn't cover most prescriptions or dental, vision, or hearing services.

As a result, most traditional Medicare enrollees buy extra coverage from private insurance companies under Medicare Part D, the prescription drug plan. Some also buy a Medigap policy that covers the costs traditional Medicare leaves behind, such as deductibles, copayments, and coinsurance.

Medicare Advantage

This year, the other half of Medicare beneficiaries opted for privately offered, all-in-one managed-care plans known as Medicare Advantage, usually including prescription drug coverage, dental, and vision. The drawbacks are smaller networks and a greater likelihood that treatments and medications will require prior authorization. Like beneficiaries in traditional Medicare, Medicare Advantage participants also pay Part B premiums.

"People really need to do their research before they enroll in Medicare, because there are trade-offs," said David Lipschutz, a co-director at the Center for Medicare Advocacy.

The hassle saves money

Every fall, insurers that offer Part D and Advantage plans send enrollees a critical document known as an Annual Notice of Change. It's a cheat sheet outlining what will be different in the following year: premiums, deductibles, covered drugs. Consumer advocates and Medicare experts say people sometimes make the costly mistake of throwing it out or filing it away without reading it. Can't find it? Call the insurer and ask for another copy.

The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services projects that the average Part D premium will increase less than $1 a month for a standalone prescription drug plan, describing the market as stable. But that average doesn't tell the whole story. An analysis by KFF, the health policy research nonprofit that includes KFF Health News, found that enrollees who stay in their prescription drug plan will see a 50% increase on average, from $34 to $51. About 10.4 million people could pay higher premiums, not including higher deductibles and coinsurance costs.

Some beneficiaries who didn't have to pay monthly premiums in recent years will begin paying for prescription drug Part D coverage in 2027. While that change follows the 2025 introduction of federal caps on out-of-pocket drug expenses, it comes as the Trump administration is ending temporary federal subsidies that helped keep premiums down. The cap on out-of-pocket expenses for prescription drugs in 2027 will be $2,400, a total enrollees can opt tospread out over the course of the year.

Juliette Cubanski, who directs the Program on Medicare Policy at KFF, said people who don't shop around could be leaving money on the table.

"It is worth it to avoid any unpleasant surprises in the form of either higher premiums or higher cost sharing for covered services in 2027," she said.

Some plans no longer offered

An estimated 4.3 million people now have to look for a new Medicare Advantage or prescription drug plan after private insurers left the market. Those who want to stay in Medicare Advantage must select new coverage, or they'll be moved to traditional Medicare automatically. For those shopping for a new plan, low monthly premiums may be appealing, but it's important to read the fine print and add up the other costs.

"There are going to be, often, increases in cost sharing and copays, increases in out-of-pocket caps, and reductions in the scope of some of the extra benefits that Medicare Advantage plans provide," Lipschutz said.

So ask: Is my prescription covered? Is my pharmacy preferred? Is my doctor in-network? What does the dental benefit actually cover?

And pay attention to the out-of-pocket maximum for the Advantage plans, Cubanski said, so you know how much you might have to shell out in 2027.

"Look at that dollar value specifically," she said.

For those moving to traditional Medicare, it won't come with a drug plan, so enrollees must sign up for a new Part D plan if they want most prescriptions covered. Enrollees who miss that step when they are first eligible may not have drug coverage for the coming year, and they may face a late-enrollment penalty on their monthly premiums for life.

When selecting a drug plan, enrollees must also tell their insurer how they want to pay, either by getting a bill in the mail or by having the cost deducted from their Social Security. If you don't pick a payment plan, you could get dropped from coverage.

If enrollees elect to leave their Medicare Advantage plans for traditional Medicare within their first year of joining Medicare, they have a guaranteed right to buy a Medigap plan, with no health screening. After that, all bets are off: Insurers in most states can turn enrollees down or charge more because of a health condition. Connecticut, Maine, Massachusetts, and New York are exceptions.

Enrollees whose Advantage plans have not been renewed — and haven't been consolidated into another plan — can switch to traditional Medicare and buy a Medigap policy without a health screening, but they need to act before March.

For shopping help, think "SHIP"

Medicare experts advise enrollees to write down all their prescription drugs, as well as any procedures planned in the next year, such as a joint replacement or dental work, to help them decide which plan will cover their needs. Call a favorite doctor's office to see whether they are in-network for the plans being considered. Remember that brokers might earn commissions, especially on Advantage plans, and might not represent every plan.

For unbiased help, every state has a federally funded State Health Insurance Assistance Program that offers free plan counseling specific to your situation, in person and over the phone. To get help, go to the website at shiphelp.org/open-enrollment, email info@shiphelp.org, or call the SHIP National Technical Assistance Center at 877-839-2675.

A SHIP counselor can also help enrollees apply for benefits that help pay for Medicare premiums and prescription drug costs, such as the Medicare Savings Programs and Medicare Part D Extra Help.

KFF Health News is a national newsroom that produces in-depth journalism about health issues and is one of the core operating programs at KFF — the independent source for health policy research, polling, and journalism.
articles.fullText:
Ежегодная открытая регистрация на Medicare, федеральная программа, которая предоставляет медицинскую страховку примерно 70 миллионам человек. Выбор покрытия является сложным и часто последовательным.

Открытая регистрация продлится до 7 декабря. План, который вы выбираете, вступает в силу 1 января на весь календарный год.

Создайте собственное меню Medicare

Medicare предоставляет медицинскую страховку людям 65 лет и старше, а также некоторым молодым людям с ограниченными возможностями или определенными заболеваниями. Но это не один план. Это больше похоже на меню «Создай свое собственное страхование».

Примерно половина бенефициаров зарегистрирована в традиционной программе Medicare, которая состоит из частей A и B. План охватывает пребывание в больнице, квалифицированную сестринскую помощь, визиты к врачу, амбулаторную помощь и профилактические обследования. Зарегистрированные лица обычно могут видеть любого поставщика медицинских услуг, который принимает Medicare, и им редко требуется одобрение для диагностических тестов, таких как МРТ и КТ. Тем не менее, в традиционной программе Medicare нет ограничений на личные расходы, и она не покрывает большинство рецептов или стоматологических, зрительных или слуховых услуг.

В результате большинство традиционных абитуриентов Medicare покупают дополнительное покрытие у частных страховых компаний в соответствии с планом отпускаемых по рецепту лекарств Medicare Part D. Некоторые также покупают политику Medigap, которая покрывает расходы, которые оставляет после себя традиционная Medicare, такие как франшизы, соплатежи и страхование.

Преимущества Medicare

В этом году другая половина бенефициаров Medicare выбрала частные планы по уходу, известные как Medicare Advantage, обычно включая покрытие рецептурных лекарств, стоматологию и зрение. Недостатками являются небольшие сети и большая вероятность того, что лечение и лекарства потребуют предварительного разрешения. Как и бенефициары в традиционном Medicare, участники Medicare Advantage также платят премии в части B.

«Люди действительно должны провести свое исследование, прежде чем они зарегистрируются в Medicare, потому что есть компромиссы», - сказал Дэвид Липшуц, содиректор Центра защиты Medicare.

Суета экономит деньги

Каждую осень страховщики, предлагающие планы Part D и Advantage, отправляют абитуриентам важный документ, известный как Ежегодное уведомление об изменениях. Это чит-лист, в котором изложено, что будет отличаться в следующем году: премии, франшизы, покрытые лекарства. Потребители и эксперты Medicare говорят, что люди иногда совершают дорогостоящую ошибку, выбрасывая или подавая его, не читая его. Не можете найти? Позвоните страховщику и попросите другую копию.

Центры Medicare & Medicaid Services прогнозируют, что средняя премия за часть D увеличится менее чем на 1 доллар в месяц для отдельного плана отпускаемых по рецепту лекарств, описывая рынок как стабильный. Но это среднее не говорит всей истории. Анализ, проведенный некоммерческой организацией KFF, занимающейся исследованиями в области политики здравоохранения, включающей KFF Health News, показал, что число абитуриентов, которые остаются в своем плане отпускаемых по рецепту лекарств, увеличится в среднем на 50% с 34 до 51 доллара. Около 10,4 миллиона человек могут платить более высокие премии, не включая более высокие франшизы и расходы на страхование.

Некоторые бенефициары, которым не приходилось платить ежемесячные премии в последние годы, начнут платить за покрытие части D в 2027 году. Хотя это изменение следует за введением в 2025 году федеральных ограничений на расходы на лекарства из своего кармана, это происходит, поскольку администрация Трампа прекращает временные федеральные субсидии, которые помогли снизить премии. Ограничение расходов на отпускаемые по рецепту лекарства в 2027 году составит 2400 долларов США, и в течение года общее число участников может распределиться.

Джульетта Кубански, которая руководит Программой по политике медицинского страхования в KFF, сказала, что люди, которые не делают покупки, могут оставлять деньги на столе.

«Стоит избегать каких-либо неприятных сюрпризов в виде более высоких премий или более высокого распределения затрат на крытые услуги в 2027 году», — сказала она.

Некоторые планы больше не предлагаются

По оценкам, 4,3 миллиона человек теперь должны искать новый план Medicare Advantage после того, как частные страховщики покинули рынок. Те, кто хочет остаться в Medicare Advantage, должны выбрать новое покрытие, или они будут переведены на традиционное Medicare автоматически. Для тех, кто покупает новый план, низкие ежемесячные премии могут быть привлекательными, но важно прочитать мелкий шрифт и сложить другие расходы.

«Часто будет происходить увеличение доли расходов и доплат, увеличение лимитов из кармана и сокращение некоторых дополнительных преимуществ, которые предоставляют планы Medicare Advantage», — сказал Липшуц.

Спрашивайте: «Моя жизнь покрыта?» Предпочтительнее ли аптека? Мой врач в сети? Что на самом деле покрывает стоматологическая польза?

И обратите внимание на максимальный из кармана для планов Advantage, сказал Кубански, поэтому вы знаете, сколько вам, возможно, придется выложить в 2027 году.

«Посмотрите на стоимость доллара», — сказала она.

Для тех, кто переезжает в традиционный Medicare, он не будет иметь плана лекарств, поэтому абитуриенты должны подписаться на новый план части D, если они хотят, чтобы большинство рецептов были покрыты. Зарегистрированные лица, которые пропускают этот шаг, когда они впервые имеют право, могут не иметь страховки от наркотиков на следующий год, и им может грозить штраф за просрочку зачисления на их ежемесячные премии за жизнь.

При выборе плана лечения наркомании, абитуриенты должны также сообщить своему страховщику, как они хотят платить, либо получая счет по почте, либо вычитая расходы из своего социального обеспечения. Если вы не выберете план оплаты, вы можете быть исключены из покрытия.

Если абитуриенты решают оставить свои планы Medicare Advantage для традиционного Medicare в течение первого года после присоединения к Medicare, они имеют гарантированное право купить план Medigap без скрининга здоровья. После этого все ставки отключены: Страховщики в большинстве штатов могут отклонить подписчиков или взимать больше из-за состояния здоровья. Коннектикут, Мэн, Массачусетс и Нью-Йорк являются исключениями.

Зарегистрированные лица, чьи планы не были обновлены и не были объединены в другой план, могут перейти на традиционный Medicare и купить политику Medigap без скрининга здоровья, но они должны действовать до марта.

Чтобы помочь с покупками, подумайте «ШИП»

Специалисты Medicare советуют регистрантам записывать все рецептурные препараты, а также любые процедуры, запланированные на следующий год, такие как замена суставов или стоматологическая работа, чтобы помочь им решить, какой план будет покрывать их потребности. Позвоните в кабинет любимого врача, чтобы узнать, находятся ли они в сети для рассмотрения планов. Помните, что брокеры могут зарабатывать комиссионные, особенно на планах Advantage, и могут не представлять каждый план.

Для беспристрастной помощи в каждом штате есть финансируемая из федерального бюджета государственная программа медицинского страхования, которая предлагает бесплатное консультирование по плану, индивидуально и по телефону. Чтобы получить помощь, перейдите на веб-сайт shiphelp.org / open-enrollment, на электронную почту info@shiphelp.org или позвоните в Национальный центр технической помощи SHIP по телефону 877-839-2675.

Консультант SHIP также может помочь абитуриентам подать заявку на льготы, которые помогают оплачивать премии Medicare и расходы на отпускаемые по рецепту лекарства, такие как программы экономии Medicare и дополнительная помощь Medicare Part D.

KFF Health News является национальным новостным отделом, который выпускает углубленную журналистику по вопросам здравоохранения и является одной из основных операционных программ в KFF - независимом источнике для исследований политики здравоохранения, опросов и журналистики.

articles.originalTitle: Why the China-ASEAN relation matters
articles.originalText: November 22 marks the fifth anniversary of the Comprehensive Strategic Partnership between China and the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN), established on the same day in 2021.
articles.originalFullText:
November 22 marks the fifth anniversary of the Comprehensive Strategic Partnership between China and the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN), established on the same day in 2021.

China and ASEAN's diplomatic relations date back to 1991, when the two first established dialogue relations at the 24th ASEAN Ministerial Meeting in Kuala Lumpur. Five years later, in 1996, their relationship was elevated to the full dialogue partnership status.

Over the decades, China-ASEAN relations have been shaped by solidarity and a shared sense of responsibility, particularly during regional challenges.

In the wake of the Asian financial crisis in 1997, China chose not to devalue its currency in a decision to prioritize regional economic stability and recovery, which was considered "a major reason why the crisis did not precipitate an even more devastating meltdown in the region," according to an economic study in 1999.

Thirty-five years after the partnership began and five years into the latest round of elevated diplomatic ties, China-ASEAN relations continue to build momentum.

From proximity to mutual prosperity

As close neighbors, China's engagement with ASEAN developed naturally.

Of ASEAN's 11 member states, three share land borders with China, and five are connected to China by the Lancang-Mekong River.

Improved infrastructure has reinforced this natural proximity. Since opening in 2021, the China-Laos Railway has linked Yunnan Province in southwest China with Vientiane, the capital of Laos, and helped cut shipping costs between the two countries by 40% to 50%, according to a World Bank report.

Transportation links are also expanding with the opening of the Pinglu Canal in 2026, a 134-kilometer waterway that connects south China's Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region to the Beibu Gulf and provides a more direct maritime route to countries including the Philippines, Malaysia and Singapore.

These geographical and infrastructure links have underpinned the economic interdependence.

Since 2009, China has been ASEAN's largest trading partner, while ASEAN has held the same position for China since 2019.

Underpinning the effort to improve connectivity is the economic complementarity, which continues to push for trade growth, said Zhai Kun, deputy director of the Institute of Area Studies and a senior research fellow at the Institute of International and Strategic Studies at Peking University.

According to Zhai, China is a key market for ASEAN's agricultural products, raw materials and manufactured goods. Meanwhile, ASEAN's consumer demand and industrial growth create opportunities for Chinese suppliers of industrial components and clean energy technologies.

Mechanism facilitates deeper cooperation

Elevating diplomatic ties with ASEAN five years ago strengthened the relationship's foundation and injected new momentum.

In the past five years, China has signed the China-ASEAN Free Trade Area (CAFTA) 3.0 Upgrade Protocol. The agreement goes beyond traditional tariff reductions and market opening, moving toward closer regulatory standards alignment.

In 2025, trade between China and ASEAN exceeded $1 trillion, up 20.1% from 2021, according to ASEAN's official website.

To have a clear blueprint for action, the two sides have also adopted the Plan of Action to Implement the China-ASEAN Comprehensive Strategic Partnership (2026-2030), which sets out key priorities and provides a roadmap for the next five years of development.

People-to-people connectivity has also reached new heights, as China rolled out the "ASEAN Visa," which made business travel among the countries even more barrier-free.

Zhai said the upgrade in diplomatic ties in 2021 was motivated by a determination to build a stronger institutional framework for closer economic ties, a strategic goal that he expects to translate into tangible benefits for people and businesses.

"Cooperation on smart customs, single window digital trade system and electronic documentation can help reduce waiting times and avoid repetitive paperwork. Coordination on standards and regulation can lower compliance costs, while cooperation in digitalization, green development and supply chains can create more opportunities for technology applications and industrial integration. Support for micro, small and medium-sized enterprises, along with technical assistance and talent development, can help more businesses seize the opportunities created by greater openness," Zhai specified.

Looking ahead, the upgraded China-ASEAN Free Trade Area (CAFTA) 3.0 is set to officially take effect in December. The two sides have also designated 2027 as the Year of China-ASEAN Cooperation on Artificial Intelligence, giving further impetus to a major area of cooperation.

22 ноября отмечается пятая годовщина Всеобъемлющего стратегического партнерства между Китаем и Ассоциацией государств Юго-Восточной Азии (АСЕАН), созданной в тот же день в 2021 году.

Дипломатические отношения между Китаем и АСЕАН начались в 1991 году, когда на 24-й Министерской встрече АСЕАН в Куала-Лумпуре были установлены первые диалоговые отношения. Пять лет спустя, в 1996 году, их отношения были возведены в статус полноценного партнерства.

На протяжении десятилетий отношения между Китаем и АСЕАН определялись солидарностью и общим чувством ответственности, особенно во время региональных проблем.

После азиатского финансового кризиса в 1997 году Китай решил не девальвировать свою валюту, приняв решение о приоритетности региональной экономической стабильности и восстановления, что считалось «основной причиной, по которой кризис не ускорил еще более разрушительный обвал в регионе», согласно экономическому исследованию 1999 года.

Спустя тридцать пять лет после начала партнерства и пять лет после последнего раунда дипломатических отношений между Китаем и АСЕАН продолжают набирать обороты.

От близости к взаимному процветанию

Будучи близкими соседями, взаимодействие Китая с АСЕАН развивалось естественным образом.

Из 11 государств-членов АСЕАН три имеют сухопутные границы с Китаем, а пять связаны с Китаем рекой Ланкан-Меконг.

Улучшенная инфраструктура усилила эту естественную близость. С момента открытия в 2021 году Китайско-Лаосская железная дорога связала провинцию Юньнань на юго-западе Китая со столицей Лаоса Вьентьяном и помогла сократить расходы на доставку между двумя странами на 40-50%.

Транспортное сообщение также расширяется с открытием канала Пинглу в 2026 году, 134-километрового водного пути, который соединяет южно-китайский автономный район Гуанси-Чжуан с заливом Бейбу и обеспечивает более прямой морской путь в страны, включая Филиппины, Малайзию и Сингапур.

Эти географические и инфраструктурные связи лежат в основе экономической взаимозависимости.

С 2009 года Китай является крупнейшим торговым партнером АСЕАН, в то время как АСЕАН занимает ту же позицию для Китая с 2019 года.

В основе усилий по улучшению взаимосвязанности лежит экономическая взаимодополняемость, которая продолжает стимулировать рост торговли, сказал Чжай Кунь, заместитель директора Института площадных исследований и старший научный сотрудник Института международных и стратегических исследований Пекинского университета.

Китай является ключевым рынком для сельскохозяйственной продукции, сырья и промышленных товаров АСЕАН. Потребительский спрос АСЕАН и промышленный рост создают возможности для китайских поставщиков промышленных компонентов и технологий чистой энергии.

Механизм способствует углублению сотрудничества

Укрепление дипломатических отношений с АСЕАН пять лет назад укрепило основы этих отношений и придало новый импульс.

За последние пять лет Китай подписал Протокол об обновлении зоны свободной торговли Китай-АСЕАН 3.0. Соглашение выходит за рамки традиционного снижения тарифов и открытия рынка, двигаясь к более тесному согласованию нормативных стандартов.

В 2025 году торговля между Китаем и АСЕАН превысила 1 триллион долларов, что на 20,1% больше, чем в 2021 году, согласно официальному сайту АСЕАН.

Чтобы иметь четкий план действий, обе стороны также приняли План действий по реализации всеобъемлющего стратегического партнерства Китай-АСЕАН (2026-2030 годы), в котором излагаются ключевые приоритеты и представлена дорожная карта на следующие пять лет развития.

Связь между людьми также достигла новых высот, поскольку Китай запустил «визу АСЕАН», которая сделала деловые поездки между странами еще более безбарьерными.

По словам Чжай, улучшение дипломатических отношений в 2021 году было мотивировано решимостью создать более прочную институциональную основу для более тесных экономических связей, стратегической целью, которую он ожидает воплотить в ощутимые выгоды для людей и бизнеса.

"Сотрудничество в области "умной" таможни, системы цифровой торговли с одним окном и электронной документации может помочь сократить время ожидания и избежать повторения бумажной работы. Координация стандартов и регулирования может снизить затраты на соблюдение нормативных требований, в то время как сотрудничество в области цифровизации, зеленого развития и цепочек поставок может создать больше возможностей для применения технологий и промышленной интеграции. Поддержка микро-, малых и средних предприятий, а также техническая помощь и развитие талантов могут помочь большему количеству предприятий воспользоваться возможностями, созданными большей открытостью.

Забегая вперед, обновленная Зона свободной торговли Китая и АСЕАН (CAFTA) 3.0 должна официально вступить в силу в декабре. Кроме того, 2027 год был объявлен Годом сотрудничества Китая и АСЕАН в области искусственного интеллекта, что придало дополнительный импульс развитию сотрудничества.

articles.originalTitle: COP31: Climate deal 'not adopted,' summit president says
articles.originalText: The summit was extended as nations worked to reach a deal, but they couldn't agree on including fossil fuels. European nations, small island states and activists have criticized oil-producing countries for the impasse.
articles.originalFullText:
What you need to know

-

Delegates from nearly 200 countries failed to reach an agreement despite prolonging the talks

-

The summit's president acknowledges that a deal was 'not adopted'

-

The final draft presented at the summit in Antalya, Turkey omitted any mention of fossil fuels

-

The EU says it cannot accept a deal that 'greenwashes fossil fuels'

-

Oil and gas consumption remains a major flashpoint amid soaring energy prices and tensions over the US-Israeli war with Iran

-

UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres said he was 'deeply disappointed' by the outcome

These are the major developments from the closing phase of the UN's COP31 Climate Summit in Antalya, Turkey, on Friday, November 20 through Sunday, November 22:

Germany says switching to clean energy would ease pressure from high fuel prices

People from all over the world are suffering due to high prices of fossil fuels, Germany's Environment Minister Carsten Schneider said after the COP31 breakdown. He added that clean technologies such as electric vehicles, heat pumps and modernizing energy industries would free the people from this dependence.

"I understand that this poses a threat to the business model of those countries that sell us oil and gas. But electrification will make the world a more peaceful and stable place," he said.

Previously, Schneider accused the oil and gas industry of dragging its feet on climate change, referencing the last-minute draft proposals which steered clear of fossil fuel phaseout.

"Some oil-producing nations realize that the situation is becoming serious for them — that is why they are blocking it so vehemently," Scheider said from Turkey.

Separately, the head of the German Environment Agency Dirk Messner said the world was divided in two camps, with some countries focusing on averting climate change and others defending oil, coal, and natural gas.

"A fossil-fuel-based economy can quickly become obsolete if the majority of countries stand together," Messner said.

He urged the nations protecting the climate to continue boosting cooperation. At the same time, Messner warned that the world would not become climate-neutral by the middle of the century without nations like Russia, Saudi Arabia and the US all supporting this goal.

"This is why the global climate dialogue must continue," he said.

EU's rejection of climate funding 'left bitter taste in many mouths,' climate campaigner tells DW

The EU's outright rejection to provide new finance commitments "set the tone" for the failed COP 31 climate summit, says Tasneem Essop, executive director at the Climate Action Network, a group over 2,500 NGOs from various parts of the world.

Talking to DW from Turkey, Essop questioned the EU's narrative of rejecting the proposed agreement for not mentioning fossil fuels.

Essop said that the EU was pushing back and obstructing discussions dealing with the issues of the Global South.

"Rich nations are responsible for providing public finance to developing countries so that they can take climate action, so that they can transition away from fossil fuels," Essop said.

"That requires financial support. And yet they came here without finance. So, it's left a bitter taste in many mouths about the action of rejection by the EU."

Essop also pointed to the UK, Australia, and European countries granting additional licenses to obtain fossil fuels.

"You can't say you're rejecting something because of fossil fuels and yet in your practice and your actions back home, you're doing exactly the opposite," she said.

She described the outcome of the summit, which went into overtime and then ended without an agreement, as "deeply disappointing."

COP31 lacked plans for developing countries, anti-fossil fuel campaigner tells DW

While oil producers like Saudi Arabia and Russia were criticized for blocking any mention fossil fuels in the draft COP31 declaration, one climate campaigner told DW that other wealthy countries also failed more vulnerable nations by not agreeing to a funded pathway for an energy transition.

Harjit Sing, strategic advisor to the Fossil Fuel Non-Proliferation Treaty Initiative said developing nations had big ambitions to turn away from oil and gas, but needed resources to do so.

"If you look at Canada, the UK, Norway, not to mention the US, they continue to expand fossil fuels, yet they point fingers towards developing countries who have a large population," Sing told DW.

"But the reality is that [the developed countries] were the ones who were blocking the conversation and the progress that we needed to create a just transition mechanism."

Sing said this lack of a funded plan for developing countries was more urgent than whether or not the final declaration mentioned fossil fuels.

"So not mentioning fossil fuels is just one part of it. The more important thing is we now need a plan, not repackaged national roadmaps, but a fair, fast and funded transition away from fossil fuels," he said.

"Fair: So rich countries move fast, [but] they are the ones who are historically responsible for the climate crisis. Fast, which is in line with science. And funded, so that developing countries get the right kind of support to make that shift."

A combination of climate change effects and insufficient funding would be "a life or death scenario" for developing countries, Sing added.

"Even at one degree temperature rise, they were facing so many disasters and we are already going to breach that 1.5 degrees Celsius of warming," he said.

Russia doubles down on fossil fuel stance, Saudi Arabia says 'all solutions' needed

After the failure of the COP31 summit over fossil fuels, Russia's delegate Sergey Kononuchenko argued that reducing the supply of oil without reducing the demand will cause "deficit, price shock and a switch to dirtier types of fuel" as well as "energy poverty," which will affect poorer countries first.

"For that reason, we cannot agree to any formulation on fossil fuel," he said.

Meanwhile, Saudi Arabia's representative referred to a last-minute proposal that called for expanding carbon capture capacities.

"We believe that climate change requires all solutions on the table," said Mohammad Ayoub, speaking for the Arab Group of nations at the summit.

"It makes no sense that solutions, concrete solutions... will be taken off the table."

While capturing carbon dioxide from the atmosphere is technically possible, critics say the technology is still in its infancy and lacks real-world infrastructure to move the needle on climate change.

Both Russia and Saudi Arabia had sought to omit any mention of fossil fuels in the final declaration, contributing the the impasse on Sunday.

UN's Guterres 'deeply disappointed' by summit

UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres said he was "deeply disappointed" by the collapse of negotiations for a joint resolution at COP31.

"I share the very profound frustration of all those who expected governments to rise to the moment the climate crisis demands," Guterres said in a statement.

"There may be no consensus in the negotiating room. There is no ambiguity in the science," he added.

"Those who profit from the destruction of our planet must never dictate the terms of the fight to save it," the UN chief said. "The continued addiction to coal, oil and gas is fueling climate chaos, exposing economies to price shocks, and undermining energy security," Guterres added.

"Major emitters must lead. Developed countries must deliver on finance. And every country must do their part."

Marshall Islands: 'We've been let down on all sides'

Marshall Islands climate envoy Kathy Jetnil-Kijiner spoke out against fossil fuel interests after the conclusion of the summit with no deal.

The Marshall Islands are a chain of volcanic atolls and coral islands numbering over 1,100 islands in total in the Pacific Ocean. Like many island nations, they are severly threatened by the effects of climate change on the earth's oceans.

"We have been let down on all sides. We were presented with the worst possible response to overshoot, a response to enhance oil and gas. We will not be forced to accept false solutions," Jetnil-Kijiner said.

"We will not compromise our future to benefit fossil fuel interests. We will not accept an outcome that undermines our security and threatens our future."

Negotiations president 'very disappointed' over collapsed talks

Australian environment minister and COP31's president of negotiations, Chris Bowen, expressed disappointment that the sweeping deal he tried to broker ultimately collapsed.

As part of a compromise between the two countries, Turkey hosted the summit while Australia took a leading role over negotiations.

"Unfortunately, we were unable to reach agreement on a cover decision... And that's disappointing. Very disappointing," said Bowen.

"An obvious issue is the transition away from fossil fuels, where some parties insisted that must be mentioned, other parties insisted that if it was mentioned they would veto."

Nevertheless, Bowen highlighted some of the ways in which the summit has still had a positive impact.

"A lot of good things happened this COP. A lot of events which told the clean energy story. A lot of commitments made — like the more than 90 countries that signed the electrification pledge, for example. And all that is good work and a great thing," he said.

COP31 fails to agree climate deal amid fossil fuel rift

The COP31 climate summit has failed to agree on a final joint declaration.

During a plenary session, the summit's Turkish president acknowledged there would be no climate deal.

"I understand that there is no agreement on this text. For that reason, these decisions have not been adopted," Murat Kurum, who is also Turkey's environment minister, told a closing plenary in the Mediterranean city of Antalya.

The rift centered on whether to include the phaseout of fossil fuels in the final declaration. Scientists say the burning of fossil fuels such as coal, oil and gas is the main cause of global warming.

European nations, smaller island states and climate activists have criticized oil-producing countries for the omission.

Ghana says COP presidency has not 'shown respect'

Several nations continued to raise serious objections to the draft.

Antwi-Boasiako Amoah, chair of the African Group of Negotiators, took a shot at the presidency for how it has handled the negotiations.

"With all due respect Mr. President, you have not shown respect to a group of 54 countries (from Africa) and my country (Ghana) for that matter," Amoah said.

Panama rejects draft decision, saying it 'should be based on science'

Panama's representative said the Central American nation was amongst those who suffer most from the consequences and issue of climate justice.

Panamanian Environment Minister Juan Carlos Navarro said the talks were being held hostage by a "petroleum mafia" and need to be reformed.

He said science must be the basis for the cover decision, adding that those who contributed to this crisis must shoulder the responsibility to deal with it.

"We are running out of time," Navarro told attendees. "Panama cannot support this decision. The planet cannot continue to wait."

EU cannot accept deal that 'greenwashes fossil fuels': Irish minister

Ireland's Climate Minister Darragh O'Brien has said the European Union is "profoundly disappointed" with the current draft deal on the table at COP31 because it "fails to meet the moment" and that the bloc will not agree to it.

"We will not endorse a cover decision that does not respond to the science, that disregards the implementation gap, and risks deepening the chasm between global commitments and the action required to correct the overshoot and bring 1.5°C within reach," O'Brien said.

"We will not endorse a cover decision that does not even mention fossil fuels, the driver of climate change. And we will not accept negotiating backward in time. And we will not accept a COP that greenwashes fossil fuels," he added.

Former Greenpeace chief says no deal is better than current deal

Former Greenpeace executive Jennifer Morgan said it would be better to end the COP31 summit with no deal than a watered-down declaration.

Her remarks come amid deep divisions over the omission of fossil fuels from the draft declaration.

Morgan rejected the notion that it would be better to accept the current draft than have no resolution at all, as the Turkish COP president has suggested.

"I think this is the day for the first time in my 31 COPs that I thought it was better not to have a decision that sets us back, that goes against what small islands and vulnerable people are saying," Morgan added.

She praised Germany for standing up to pressures to accept the current deal.

"Of course it would have been better to have a strong outcome here with everyone moving forward, but I agree with the German minister who just said if the text stays the way that it is, then it should not be accepted," Morgan said.

The US climate activist blamed oil-producing nations for the impasse.

"Saudi Arabia's fingerprints are all over" the current draft proposal, she said.

The omission has created a deadlock at COP31, which was due to conclude on Friday but has been extended as delegates seek consensus.

Morgan also blamed this year's Turkish presidency for failing to bring everybody together and instead letting countries that rely on fossil fuels dictate the terms of the agreement.

"Last year we had Brazil with a very strong presidency. They worked all year to bring countries together and they managed. It was not easy last year," Morgan said.

"This year we had presidencies that, in my view, were not well prepared. They did not bring countries together (...) it's been shuttle diplomacy with no text for four days. That's not the way you get an agreement here," she added.

Germany rejects 'unacceptable' draft deal

German Environment Minister Carsten Schneider has said the latest version of the draft agreement is "not acceptable."

Schneider said that the draft decision "not only fails to provide an adequate response but actually takes a step backward. A step backward from previous decisions on climate protection is the last thing Germany can support."

Schneider said that delegates had been working hard for days to reach a unanimous decision on "the world's greatest challenge: human-induced climate change," noting that this summer had "shown that the nature of this warming not only costs lives — as in Nepal — but also changes our world for the worse."

"It is up to us, as humanity, to do something about it. That is why a conference dedicated to climate protection — whose sole purpose is to protect the climate — must send a clear signal that we are taking action against this threat."

Schneider said he still believed most nations are willing to work to enact climate protection, but singled out those who still rely on fossil fuels to power their economies.

"The overwhelming majority of nations are committed to climate protection. Some, however, are still making huge profits from oil and gas and are unwilling to scale back their production or to pioneer a clear roadmap for reducing greenhouse gas emissions in this area," he added.

France criticizes draft deal as 'backward' step

France has called a new draft deal proposed at COP31 a "backward" step.

French Ecological Transition Minister Monique Barbut criticized the deal for failing to mention fossil fuels, casting fresh uncertainty over whether nations will be able to reach an agreement.

"Time is ticking and we are not there yet," French Ecological Transition Minister Monique Barbut said in a statement.

Turkish COP31 president calls for resolution to be adopted

COP31 President Murat Kurum has expressed his frustration over the deadlock at the summit.

The latest version of the draft deal again fails to mention fossil fuels, the main cause of global warming.

Over 40 hours after its scheduled conclusion and with no compromise in sight, the summit risks losing the numbers required to make any decision as delegates leave for home.

"If it is not adopted, I believe those who push the COP process into a deadlock will need to reflect on their position," Kurum said.

"It is our wish that this resolution be passed. We shall shortly be expressing our determination to ensure that this resolution is passed at the general meeting," he said.

"It is up to the parties involved. If there is sincerity here, and if there is a genuine desire to get things done, I believe that this can be achieved in this chamber. We shall see about that in a moment," Kurum added.

UN's Guterres 'deeply disappointed' by summit

UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres said he was "deeply disappointed" by the collapse of negotiations for a joint resolution at COP31.

"I share the very profound frustration of all those who expected governments to rise to the moment the climate crisis demands," Guterres said in a statement.

"There may be no consensus in the negotiating room. There is no ambiguity in the science," he added.

"Those who profit from the destruction of our planet must never dictate the terms of the fight to save it," the UN chief said. "The continued addiction to coal, oil and gas is fueling climate chaos, exposing economies to price shocks, and undermining energy security," Guterres added.

"Major emitters must lead. Developed countries must deliver on finance. And every country must do their part."

Marshall Islands: 'We've been let down on all sides'

Marshall Islands climate envoy Kathy Jetnil-Kijiner spoke out against fossil fuel interests after the conclusion of the summit with no deal.

The Marshall Islands are a chain of volcanic atolls and coral islands numbering over 1,100 islands in total in the Pacific Ocean. Like many island nations, they are severly threatened by the effects of climate change on the earth's oceans.

"We have been let down on all sides. We were presented with the worst possible response to overshoot, a response to enhance oil and gas. We will not be forced to accept false solutions," Jetnil-Kijiner said.

"We will not compromise our future to benefit fossil fuel interests. We will not accept an outcome that undermines our security and threatens our future."

Negotiations president 'very disappointed' over collapsed talks

Australian environment minister and COP31's president of negotiations, Chris Bowen, expressed disappointment that the sweeping deal he tried to broker ultimately collapsed.

As part of a compromise between the two countries, Turkey hosted the summit while Australia took a leading role over negotiations.

"Unfortunately, we were unable to reach agreement on a cover decision... And that's disappointing. Very disappointing," said Bowen.

"An obvious issue is the transition away from fossil fuels, where some parties insisted that must be mentioned, other parties insisted that if it was mentioned they would veto."

Nevertheless, Bowen highlighted some of the ways in which the summit has still had a positive impact.

"A lot of good things happened this COP. A lot of events which told the clean energy story. A lot of commitments made — like the more than 90 countries that signed the electrification pledge, for example. And all that is good work and a great thing," he said.

COP31 fails to agree climate deal amid fossil fuel rift

The COP31 climate summit has failed to agree on a final joint declaration.

During a plenary session, the summit's Turkish president acknowledged there would be no climate deal.

"I understand that there is no agreement on this text. For that reason, these decisions have not been adopted," Murat Kurum, who is also Turkey's environment minister, told a closing plenary in the Mediterranean city of Antalya.

The rift centered on whether to include the phaseout of fossil fuels in the final declaration. Scientists say the burning of fossil fuels such as coal, oil and gas is the main cause of global warming.

European nations, smaller island states and climate activists have criticized oil-producing countries for the omission.

Ghana says COP presidency has not 'shown respect'

Several nations continued to raise serious objections to the draft.

Antwi-Boasiako Amoah, chair of the African Group of Negotiators, took a shot at the presidency for how it has handled the negotiations.

"With all due respect Mr. President, you have not shown respect to a group of 54 countries (from Africa) and my country (Ghana) for that matter," Amoah said.

Panama rejects draft decision, saying it 'should be based on science'

Panama's representative said the Central American nation was amongst those who suffer most from the consequences and issue of climate justice.

Panamanian Environment Minister Juan Carlos Navarro said the talks were being held hostage by a "petroleum mafia" and need to be reformed.

He said science must be the basis for the cover decision, adding that those who contributed to this crisis must shoulder the responsibility to deal with it.

"We are running out of time," Navarro told attendees. "Panama cannot support this decision. The planet cannot continue to wait."

EU cannot accept deal that 'greenwashes fossil fuels': Irish minister

Ireland's Climate Minister Darragh O'Brien has said the European Union is "profoundly disappointed" with the current draft deal on the table at COP31 because it "fails to meet the moment" and that the bloc will not agree to it.

"We will not endorse a cover decision that does not respond to the science, that disregards the implementation gap, and risks deepening the chasm between global commitments and the action required to correct the overshoot and bring 1.5°C within reach," O'Brien said.

"We will not endorse a cover decision that does not even mention fossil fuels, the driver of climate change. And we will not accept negotiating backward in time. And we will not accept a COP that greenwashes fossil fuels," he added.

Former Greenpeace chief says no deal is better than current deal

Former Greenpeace executive Jennifer Morgan said it would be better to end the COP31 summit with no deal than a watered-down declaration.

Her remarks come amid deep divisions over the omission of fossil fuels from the draft declaration.

Morgan rejected the notion that it would be better to accept the current draft than have no resolution at all, as the Turkish COP president has suggested.

"I think this is the day for the first time in my 31 COPs that I thought it was better not to have a decision that sets us back, that goes against what small islands and vulnerable people are saying," Morgan added.

She praised Germany for standing up to pressures to accept the current deal.

"Of course it would have been better to have a strong outcome here with everyone moving forward, but I agree with the German minister who just said if the text stays the way that it is, then it should not be accepted," Morgan said.

The US climate activist blamed oil-producing nations for the impasse.

"Saudi Arabia's fingerprints are all over" the current draft proposal, she said.

The omission has created a deadlock at COP31, which was due to conclude on Friday but has been extended as delegates seek consensus.

Morgan also blamed this year's Turkish presidency for failing to bring everybody together and instead letting countries that rely on fossil fuels dictate the terms of the agreement.

"Last year we had Brazil with a very strong presidency. They worked all year to bring countries together and they managed. It was not easy last year," Morgan said.

"This year we had presidencies that, in my view, were not well prepared. They did not bring countries together (...) it's been shuttle diplomacy with no text for four days. That's not the way you get an agreement here," she added.

Germany rejects 'unacceptable' draft deal

German Environment Minister Carsten Schneider has said the latest version of the draft agreement is "not acceptable."

Schneider said that the draft decision "not only fails to provide an adequate response but actually takes a step backward. A step backward from previous decisions on climate protection is the last thing Germany can support."

Schneider said that delegates had been working hard for days to reach a unanimous decision on "the world's greatest challenge: human-induced climate change," noting that this summer had "shown that the nature of this warming not only costs lives — as in Nepal — but also changes our world for the worse."

"It is up to us, as humanity, to do something about it. That is why a conference dedicated to climate protection — whose sole purpose is to protect the climate — must send a clear signal that we are taking action against this threat."

Schneider said he still believed most nations are willing to work to enact climate protection, but singled out those who still rely on fossil fuels to power their economies.

"The overwhelming majority of nations are committed to climate protection. Some, however, are still making huge profits from oil and gas and are unwilling to scale back their production or to pioneer a clear roadmap for reducing greenhouse gas emissions in this area," he added.

France criticizes draft deal as 'backward' step

France has called a new draft deal proposed at COP31 a "backward" step.

French Ecological Transition Minister Monique Barbut criticized the deal for failing to mention fossil fuels, casting fresh uncertainty over whether nations will be able to reach an agreement.

"Time is ticking and we are not there yet," French Ecological Transition Minister Monique Barbut said in a statement.

Turkish COP31 president calls for resolution to be adopted

COP31 President Murat Kurum has expressed his frustration over the deadlock at the summit.

The latest version of the draft deal again fails to mention fossil fuels, the main cause of global warming.

Over 40 hours after its scheduled conclusion and with no compromise in sight, the summit risks losing the numbers required to make any decision as delegates leave for home.

"If it is not adopted, I believe those who push the COP process into a deadlock will need to reflect on their position," Kurum said.

"It is our wish that this resolution be passed. We shall shortly be expressing our determination to ensure that this resolution is passed at the general meeting," he said.

"It is up to the parties involved. If there is sincerity here, and if there is a genuine desire to get things done, I believe that this can be achieved in this chamber. We shall see about that in a moment," Kurum added.

articles.originalTitle: Swiss vice president, foreign minister to visit China
articles.originalText: Swiss Vice President and Foreign Minister Ignazio Cassis will visit China from November 23 to 24 and hold the fifth round of the China-Switzerland Foreign Ministers' Strategic Dialogue, a Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson announced.
articles.originalFullText:
Vice President of the Swiss Federal Council and Head of the Federal Department of Foreign Affairs Ignazio Cassis will visit China from November 23 to 24 and hold the fifth round of the China-Switzerland Foreign Ministers' Strategic Dialogue, a Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson announced on Sunday.

The visit comes at the invitation of Wang Yi, a member of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and minister of foreign affairs, the spokesperson said.

articles.originalTitle: Bayern Munich bosses under fire over Jamal Musiala comments
articles.originalText: Officials have publicly questioned whether Musiala will ever fully recover from a debilitating neurological condition and queried the validity of his contract, prompting criticism from fans, media and the FIFPRO union.
articles.originalFullText:
In the space of just two days this weekend, Bayern Munich were held to a 1-1 draw by FC Cologne, saw Ballon d'Or winner Harry Kane ruled out until the new year with a serious ankle injury and lost first place in the Bundesliga to rivals Borussia Dortmund.

But even those setbacks – as well as the return of head coach Vincent Kompany to the sideline following health issues – have been overshadowed by explosive public comments made by Bayern club bosses regarding young attacker and Germany international Jamal Musiala.

What is wrong with Jamal Musiala?

Back in July 2025, Musiala suffered a fractured fibula and a broken ankle at the Club World Cup.

Since then, the 23-year-old has been battling to recover not only from that injury but also with a debilitating neurological condition diagnosed as "absence seizures" which led him to collapse on the pitch in two consecutive pre-season games in August this year.

Musiala has struggled to replicate the sort of form which led to a well-remunerated contract extension in January 2025, prior to the ankle injury and the seizures.

The situation has now prompted a series of controversial public remarks from the Bayern hierarchy seemingly questioning the validity of that contract.

What have Bayern Munich officials said?

"It is well known that he has a contract which contains some considerable sums," former chief executive and current supervisory board member Karl-Heinz Rummenigge told broadcaster Sky on Friday evening following the 1-1 draw with Cologne, in which Musiala had made a 20-minute substitute appearance.

"It's in all of our interest that he comes back, ideally in top form, but what happens if that's not the case?" asked Rummenigge, adding that Musiala's condition "leads us to suspect, unfortunately, that it will be difficult [for him] to return to the level that he has often shown in this stadium" and that "then we of course have to think about the finances."

Rummenigge suggested a need for Bayern to hold talks with Musiala, his family and his representatives because "such sums are, with respect, no longer justifiable."

Asked whether Bayern would consider selling Musiala, Rummenigge said he considered it unlikely that any club would be prepared to buy the player out of his new contract, which is set to run until 2030 and which reportedly sees Musiala earn up to €30 million per year.

"I cannot imagine that Jamal would leave the club or that any other club would buy him under these conditions," said Rummenigge. "And that is a problem."

Rummenigge was not the first senior Bayern official to express such doubts. Earlier this month, former club president Uli Hoeness had told local broadcaster Bayrischer Rundfunk that Musiala's situation presented the club with a "dilemma."

"He has an illness which cannot be cured but which can be somewhat controlled through medication," said Hoeness, who also sits on Bayern's supervisory board, questioning "whether he will ever regain the ability he once had" and stating that "he continues to receive money."

Bayern chief executive Jan-Christian Dreesen has also weighed in, telling Munich's Abendzeitung newspaper last week: "We all have a responsibility towards the club and we all hope that Jamal will come back. Of course this will take time. We will assess the situation and speak to his family and management. Either we'll all be happy that the old Jamal [will return] or, if he becomes a different [player], we'll have to hold talks."

FIFPRO: 'Bayern should know better'

The comments by Hoeness, Dreesen and Rummenigge landed like a bombshell in Germany and beyond.

The global players' union FIFPRO issued a statement on Saturday slamming what they called "a coordinated strategy to put pressure on Musiala and his representatives ahead of any negotiations," highlighting Bayern's "duty of care" towards their player, and stating: "A club of Bayern's standing should know better."

"Across professional football, uncertainty about a player's future can take a toll on their mental health, particularly when they are recovering from injury," the statement continued. "Making Musiala's health and future a matter of public debate adds to that pressure. Contracts are there to be respected. An injury or a dip in form gives a club no grounds to reopen terms it agreed to, just as a run of outstanding performances gives a player no automatic right to a pay rise."

Former Bayern Munich and Germany defender Lothar Matthäus also criticized the club, saying in his role as a pundit for Sky: "I've been a bit shocked throughout the entire week. It started with Uli Hoeness, continued with Jan-Christian Dreesen, and yesterday Karl-Heinz Rummenigge chose the strongest words of all. I have enormous respect for Karl-Heinz. I've known him for over 30 years. But he chose those statements very deliberately. The person who suffers most from all this is Jamal Musiala."

The comments by the Bayern bosses also came just hours ahead of the club's annual general meeting on Saturday, where club members – who hold a majority 70% stake in the club in accordance with German football's "50+1" ownership rule – took to the stand to criticize the club's hierarchy.

One member, professional neurologist Jonatan Hoffmann, expressed his "absolute respect" for Musiala and said that patients suffering from such conditions require "support."

He said Musiala had received such support from head coach Vincent Kompany and director of sport Max Eberl, but said Hoeness', Dreesen's and Rummenigge's comments were "not helpful" and had "little to do with the much talked about Bayern Munich family" – earning considerable applause from fellow members.

Bayern president: 'Musiala will get time and support'

Bayern president Herbert Hainer, the club's most senior elected official, attempted to deescalate the situation, responding to Hoffmann by saying: "Health and difficult situations are fundamentally always taken into account at FC Bayern."

Indeed, Bayern have recently been praised for their considerate handling of captain Joshua Kimmich following the unexpected death of his father, and of head coach Kompany, who returned to the touchline against Cologne on Friday following a month-long absence after collapsing due to a particularly serious viral infection.

"When it comes to Jamal, we all want the old Jamal back as he was before his injury," said Hainer. "And he will receive all the support and time he needs from the club."

Speaking on the sidelines of the meeting, chief executive Dreesen also attempted to row back on his comments, insisting to reporters that he and his colleagues had not been trying to put Musiala under pressure.

"We all want Jamal to return to the old Jamal. He needs time. We've said that several times. And he must get that. And then we'll see how things look in the new year," he said, adding that there was no need "to talk about the contract."

President Hainer also dismissed questions from journalists as to whether Bayern felt they had been misled by Musiala's agents before offering him a new contract, inferring that the player's representatives may have known about his neurological condition.

"I absolutely do not think that anyone knew beforehand," Hainer insisted.

German media criticize Bayern

But the public criticism has continued. Leading German sports publication Kicker said it was understandable for the Bayern bosses to be frustrated but called their approach "irresponsible" and said their anger "harms the wrong person" in Musiala.

"He can't help his injuries or neurological condition," wrote editor-in-chief Matthias Dersch. "Musiala is only 23 … and is in the most difficult phase of his career. We cannot imagine how he must be feeling, his insecurities and perhaps also fears about his health and his future. And no: the amount of money he earns is no cure."

German football magazine 11Freunde said the Musiala case offered "a glimpse into the abyss of professional football … an unembellished look behind the scenes of a business which is generally portrayed only as glamorous and exciting … into a shadow world where human beings are damned to function … where the value of a person is measured only by their ability to perform over and over again … That's football: capitalism in its purest form."

Meanwhile, the business of football continues. Borussia Dortmund capitalized on Bayern's draw to go top of the Bundesliga with a 1-0 win away at Borussia Mönchengladbach, Harry Kane underwent an operation on a torn ankle ligament but will be out until the new year, meaning he will miss Bayern's trip to Lille in the Champions League on Wednesday.

And the young Jamal Musiala will continue to battle the effects of serious physical and neurological conditions.
articles.fullText:
Всего за два дня в эти выходные «Бавария» провела вничью со счетом 1:1 ФК «Кельн», победитель «Золотого мяча» Гарри Кейн исключил до нового года серьезную травму лодыжки и уступил первое место в Бундеслиге соперникам «Боруссии» Дортмунд.

Но даже эти неудачи, а также возвращение главного тренера Винсента Компани на обочину после проблем со здоровьем, были омрачены взрывными публичными комментариями боссов клуба «Бавария» в отношении молодого нападающего и международного игрока Германии Джамаля Мусиалы.

Что не так с Джамалем Мусила?

Еще в июле 2025 года Мусиала получил перелом фибулы и сломанную лодыжку на клубном чемпионате мира.

С тех пор 23-летний футболист борется за восстановление не только после травмы, но и с изнурительным неврологическим состоянием, которое было диагностировано как «припадки отсутствия», что привело его к краху на поле в двух предсезонных играх подряд в августе этого года.

Мусиала изо всех сил пытался воспроизвести форму, которая привела к хорошо оплачиваемому продлению контракта в январе 2025 года, до травмы лодыжки и судорог.

Ситуация вызвала ряд противоречивых публичных замечаний со стороны иерархии Баварии, которые, по-видимому, ставят под сомнение действительность этого контракта.

Что сказали чиновники «Баварии»?

«Хорошо известно, что у него есть контракт, который содержит некоторые значительные суммы», - сказал бывший исполнительный директор и нынешний член наблюдательного совета Карл-Хайнц Румменигге в эфире телеканала Sky в пятницу вечером после ничьей 1-1 с Кельном, в которой Мусиала появился на 20-минутной замене.

«Во всех наших интересах, чтобы он вернулся, в идеале в лучшей форме, но что произойдет, если это не так?» — спросил Румменигге, добавив, что состояние Мусиалы «приводит нас к подозрению, к сожалению, что ему будет трудно вернуться на тот уровень, который он часто показывал на этом стадионе» и что «тогда мы, конечно, должны думать о финансах».

Румменигге предложил Баварии провести переговоры с Мусиалой, его семьей и его представителями, потому что «такие суммы, с уважением, больше не оправданы».

Отвечая на вопрос о том, рассмотрит ли «Бавария» вопрос о продаже «Мусиалы», Румменигге сказал, что он считает маловероятным, что какой-либо клуб будет готов выкупить игрока из его нового контракта, который будет действовать до 2030 года и который, как сообщается, заработает до 30 миллионов евро в год.

«Я не могу себе представить, что Джамал покинет клуб или что какой-либо другой клуб купит его на этих условиях», — сказал Румменигге. «И это проблема».

Румменигге не был первым высокопоставленным чиновником «Баварии», выразившим подобные сомнения. Ранее в этом месяце бывший президент клуба Ули Хёнесс сказал местному вещателю Bayrischer Rundfunk, что ситуация с Мусиалой подарила клубу «дилемму».

«У него есть болезнь, которую нельзя вылечить, но которую можно несколько контролировать с помощью лекарств», — сказал Хонесс, который также входит в наблюдательный совет «Баварии», задаваясь вопросом, «будет ли он когда-нибудь восстанавливать свои способности, которые когда-то имел».

Генеральный директор «Баварии» Ян-Кристиан Дрисен также высказался в интервью мюнхенской газете Abendzeitung на прошлой неделе: «Мы все несем ответственность перед клубом и надеемся, что Джамал вернется. Конечно, это займет время. Мы оценим ситуацию и поговорим с его семьей и руководством. Либо мы все будем рады, что старый Джамал вернется, либо, если он станет другим игроком, нам придется вести переговоры».

ФИФПРО: "Бавария должна знать лучше"

Комментарии Хенесса, Дрисена и Румменигге приземлились как бомба в Германии и за ее пределами.

Профсоюз глобальных игроков FIFPRO в субботу выступил с заявлением, в котором осудил то, что они назвали «скоординированной стратегией оказания давления на Мусиалу и его представителей перед любыми переговорами», подчеркнув «обязанность Баварии заботиться» о своем игроке и заявив: «Клуб Баварии должен лучше знать».

«В профессиональном футболе неуверенность в будущем игрока может негативно сказаться на его психическом здоровье, особенно когда он восстанавливается после травмы», — говорится в заявлении. «Придание здоровью и будущему Мусиалы статуса предмета публичных дебатов усиливает это давление. Контракты должны соблюдаться. Травма или падение формы не дают клубу никаких оснований для возобновления условий, на которые он согласился, так же как серия выдающихся выступлений не дает игроку автоматического права на повышение зарплаты».

Бывший защитник «Баварии» и Германии Лотар Маттеус также раскритиковал клуб, заявив в роли эксперта по Sky: «Я был немного шокирован на протяжении всей недели. Все началось с Ули Хёнесса, продолжил Ян-Кристиан Дрисен, а вчера Карл-Хайнц Румменигге выбрал самые сильные слова из всех. Я очень уважаю Карла-Хайнца. Я знаю его более 30 лет. Но он выбрал эти заявления очень сознательно. Больше всего от всего этого страдает Джамал Мусиала».

Комментарии боссов «Баварии» также прозвучали всего за несколько часов до ежегодного общего собрания клуба в субботу, где члены клуба, которые владеют большинством в 70% акций клуба в соответствии с правилом владения немецким футболом «50+1», выступили с критикой иерархии клуба.

Один из членов, профессиональный невролог Йонатан Хоффманн, выразил «абсолютное уважение» к Мусиале и сказал, что пациенты, страдающие от таких состояний, нуждаются в «поддержке».

Он сказал, что Мусиала получил такую поддержку от главного тренера Винсента Компани и директора по спорту Макса Эберла, но сказал, что комментарии Хенесса, Дрейзена и Румменигге были «не полезными» и «не имели ничего общего с много разговорами о семье Баварии в Мюнхене».

Президент "Баварии": "Музыала получит время и поддержку"

Президент «Баварии» Герберт Хайнер, самый высокопоставленный выборный чиновник клуба, попытался деэскалировать ситуацию, отвечая Хоффману, сказав: «Здоровье и сложные ситуации в корне всегда учитываются в «Баварии».

Действительно, недавно «Баварию» похвалили за внимательное отношение к капитану Джошуа Киммичу после неожиданной смерти его отца и главного тренера Компани, который вернулся на линию соприкосновения с Кельном в пятницу после месячного отсутствия после коллапса из-за особенно серьезной вирусной инфекции.

«Когда дело доходит до Джамаля, мы все хотим, чтобы старый Джамал вернулся таким, каким он был до травмы», — сказал Хайнер. И он получит всю необходимую поддержку и время от клуба.

Выступая в кулуарах встречи, исполнительный директор Дрисен также попытался отозваться от своих комментариев, настаивая на том, что он и его коллеги не пытались оказать давление на Мусилалу.

"Мы все хотим, чтобы Джамал вернулся в старый Джамал. Ему нужно время. Мы говорили это несколько раз. И он должен получить это. А потом посмотрим, как будет выглядеть в новом году, - сказал он, добавив, что говорить о контракте не было необходимости.

Президент Хайнер также отклонил вопросы журналистов о том, чувствовала ли «Бавария», что агенты Мусиалы ввели их в заблуждение, прежде чем предложить ему новый контракт, что означает, что представители игрока, возможно, знали о его неврологическом состоянии.

«Я абсолютно не думаю, что кто-то знал заранее», — настаивал Хайнер.

Немецкие СМИ критикуют Баварию

Но общественная критика продолжается. Ведущее немецкое спортивное издание Kicker заявило, что для боссов «Баварии» понятно, что они разочарованы, но назвало их подход «безответственным» и сказало, что их гнев «наносит вред не тому человеку» в Мусиале.

«Он не может помочь своим травмам или неврологическому состоянию», — написал главный редактор Маттиас Дерш. «Музиале всего 23 года... и он находится в самой сложной фазе своей карьеры. Мы не можем себе представить, как он себя чувствует, как он неуверен в себе и, возможно, боится за свое здоровье и будущее. И нет: сумма денег, которую он зарабатывает, не является лекарством».

Немецкий футбольный журнал 11Freunde заявил, что дело Мусиалы предлагает «проблеск в бездну профессионального футбола ... неприкрашенный взгляд за кулисами бизнеса, который обычно изображается только как гламурный и захватывающий ... в теневой мир, где человеческие существа прокляты, чтобы функционировать ... где ценность человека измеряется только их способностью выполнять снова и снова ... Это футбол: капитализм в чистом виде».

Между тем, бизнес футбола продолжается. Боруссия Дортмунд капитализировалась на ничьей Баварии, чтобы пойти на вершину Бундеслиги с победой 1:0 в Боруссии Мёнхенгладбах, Гарри Кейн перенес операцию на разорванной связке лодыжки, но будет выходить до нового года, что означает, что он пропустит поездку Баварии в Лигу чемпионов в среду.

Молодой Джамал Мусиала продолжит борьбу с серьезными физическими и неврологическими заболеваниями.
